narrative.summary: Sierra Leone has no AI law or AI-specific regulation. Its only official AI policy text is the AI pillar of the National Innovation and Digital Strategy 2019-2029, which proposes using the country as an 'AI lab' and applying AI to governance. The communications ministry is developing a first National AI Strategy with the World Bank, and a data protection bill is still pending.

narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026. Parliament's and the central bank's websites could not be accessed, nor could one 2021 Gazette issue that mentions artificial intelligence. The National AI Strategy, an AI readiness report and the data protection bill are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Sierra Leone National Innovation & Digital Strategy 2019 - 2029: Digitization for all: Identity, Economy, and Governance
instruments.english_title: Sierra Leone National Innovation and Digital Strategy (NIDS) 2019-2029
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Sierra Leone (developed by the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation, Office of the President)
instruments.current_status: Ten-year strategy (2019-2029); the document's pages state 'Last Updated: November 1st, 2019'. It is currently hosted by the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation, which in May 2026 was developing Sierra Leone's first dedicated National AI Strategy with the World Bank (see leads); NIDS is not stated to be superseded.
instruments.summary: Sierra Leone's ten-year digital strategy, built on three pillars (digital identity, digital economy, digital governance), with 'Country-as-AI-Lab' as a guiding principle: the country is to serve as a platform for applied AI and data-science research for governance, using a human-in-the-loop approach that explicitly cites the risk of AI trained on biased historical data. Its short-term 'Applied AI for Governance' activity sets out AI uses in education, planning and development, healthcare and justice (e.g. diagnostic support, anomaly detection against corruption). It also calls for a statutory Information System Authority to set public-sector data and security standards and a data protection body to mediate disputes over personal data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national strategy with an explicit AI pillar (Country-as-AI-Lab, Applied AI for Governance); precursor to the National AI Strategy under development.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Sierra Leone's legislation and gazette portal, the communications ministry, other ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for binding law, government AI governance, ethics, risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, data and privacy, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sectoral rules, generative AI, drafts, international agreements or historical publications. Parliament's and the central bank's sites and one 2021 gazette notice were unavailable, the health and justice ministries were not searched separately, and the national AI strategy, an AI readiness diagnostic and the data protection bill are listed as leads.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. parliament.gov.sl self-signed TLS; bsl.gov.sl proxy 502; Gazette No. 54 (10 Sep 2021, p.5) Cloudflare/403 - snippet looks like an objects clause, not an AI instrument. MoH/MoJ sites not searched separately. NIDS dated 2019 ('last updated 1 Nov 2019'); data-privacy category dropped at merge. Digital Development Strategy 2022, Policy 2021, Data Strategy 2023 mention AI only in passing (not recorded). Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: SierraLII (gov.sl legislation and gazette portal) searched for AI, automated decision, deepfake, algorithm, data protection: no AI law or AI provision in any Act found. Cyber Security and Crime Act 2021, National Communications Authority Act 2022 and Electronic Transactions Bill 2019 (MoCTI copies) contain no AI provisions. One gazette hit (No. 54, 10 Sept 2021, p.5) could not be opened. Parliament site failed TLS. No data protection act in force; DP bill held as lead.; Government: MoCTI site and media library fully searched: NIDS 2019-2029 recorded; National Digital Development Strategy (Dec 2022), Digital Development Policy 2021, National Data Strategy 2023, Cybersecurity Strategy and Policy read: only passing AI mentions, not recorded. National AI Strategy and AI Readiness Diagnostic held as leads. No public-sector AI/GenAI guideline found (MoU with Qhala and civil-servant AI training are news only).; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: MoICE (news only), MBSSE (education), DSTI site; no ministry-level AI documents.; Regulators: Searched, nothing found: NatCA (telecom), NC3/nccc.gov.sl (cyber); Bank of Sierra Leone site unreachable (proxy 502). No data protection authority exists yet.. Not reached: Parliament of Sierra Leone website (TLS certificate failure); Bank of Sierra Leone website (proxy 502); Sierra Leone Gazette No. 54 of 10 September 2021 full text (Cloudflare challenge / 403 on both curl and WebFetch); Ministry of Health and Ministry of Justice sites (not searched separately; time box). Could not verify: Gazette No. 54 of 10 September 2021, p.5 contains 'To promote the use and development of modern technologies including artificial intelligence ... services in telecommunication and modern technology' - looks like an objects clause (likely a company/organisation notice), not a government AI instrument, but full text could not be opened.; Status of the Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill 2025 after Cabinet's April 2026 policy approval (MoICE site 503; Parliament site TLS failure).. binding-law, government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

leads.title: Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, 2025
leads.english_title: Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, 2025
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information and Civic Education
leads.note: Pending bill. Final national validation concluded 7 November 2025 (MoICE post); Cabinet approved a National Data Protection Policy and a reform merging data protection and access-to-information functions in one authority, announced 21 April 2026 (MoICE post, moice.gov.sl/?p=2375, unreachable 503 on 11 October 2026). No bill text in Parliament or the Gazette found; no National Data Protection Policy PDF located on moice.gov.sl. Sierra Leone has no data protection act in force. https://moice.gov.sl/moice-concludes-final-national-validation-of-the-data-protection-and-right-to-access-information-bill-2025/
